headline: Oil prices fell fast in early November as the US-Iran war seemed to cool, but ships near Iran still aren't safe.
summary: Oil averaged $125 a barrel in October, the highest since 2008. Then it dropped in November after the US signaled no new strikes on Iran. Gold and silver slid because traders expect US interest rates to go up. In food, sugar keeps rising because of El Niño and weather, while grain prices eased.

items.title: Oil drops about a fifth in November as war fears ease
items.text: In October, oil averaged $125 a barrel, 93% more than a year before. In November it fell about 20%. President Trump said new attacks on Iran were unlikely, and the US kept its blockade of Iran in place instead, CNBC reported. The world's energy watchdog (IEA) expects more oil than buyers need. But the danger isn't over. Both sides said ships were hit near the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane a lot of the world's oil passes through. A peace deal could push oil lower. More fighting could send it back up.

sources.name: CNBC
sources.quote: WTI is down 16% in November, and Brent has lost 20%.

sources.name: CNBC
sources.quote: an International Energy Agency report pointing to a rise in the global oil surplus

items.title: Gold and silver slide as US interest rates look set to rise
items.text: On 16 November, gold was about $3,870 an ounce and silver about $47. Both are far below their highs this year: gold averaged $5,020 in February, and silver $92.10 in January. US prices rose faster than expected, and officials at the Fed (the US central bank) talked tough. Traders now see an 85% chance the Fed raises interest rates in December, CNBC reported. Higher rates make gold and silver less attractive, because they don't pay interest.

sources.name: CNBC
sources.quote: Markets see an 85% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December

items.title: World food prices dip, but sugar keeps rising
items.text: The FAO Food Price Index dipped in October, after rising through the summer. It's still 6% higher than a year ago. Sugar went the other way: up 6.6% in a month and 28% in three months. El Niño is the main worry. NOAA, the US weather agency, says there's about a 60% chance it becomes the strongest since records began in 1950. Dry weather in Asia hurts sugar first. Palm oil usually feels it 6 to 12 months later.

sources.name: FAO
sources.quote: The FAO Sugar Price Index averaged 121.3 points in October, up 7.5 points (6.6 percent) from September

sources.name: NOAA
sources.quote: are now ~60% for the October-December and November-January periods

items.title: The US expects less corn, but the world has plenty of wheat
items.text: In its November report, the US farm department (USDA) lowered its guess for the US corn crop. It also lowered how much corn and soybeans will be left in storage. That usually pushes those prices up. It raised its guess for the world's stored wheat, partly thanks to a bigger world harvest. Wheat averaged $317 a ton in October: 8.6% less than in September, but still 37% more than a year ago. Plenty of stored grain is one reason food prices have stayed calmer than oil this year.

sources.name: DTN
sources.quote: Wheat world ending stocks were estimated at 280.82 million metric tons, up from 276.04 mmt in October.
